mainTopic: Whether a defect after שחיטה disqualifies a קרבן, the dispute over blemishes of the testicles, and a new משנה on blemishes of the pouch and tail.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about an animal missing a part. The גמרא decides that a defect before קבלה disqualifies a קרבן, but a defect after קבלה does not. It reads the ברייתא about the קרבן פסח as requiring only the age rule all the way to זריקה, and it supports this with רבי יהושע's כזית rule. From that ברייתא, רבא learns that age for קדשים is counted to the exact hour. Next the גמרא suggests that the question of an internal lack is a dispute of תנאים about bruised, crushed, torn and cut testicles. רבי יוסי's split view rules that out, so the גמרא explains the dispute as being about visible blemishes. A new משנה then lists blemishes of the pouch, a female's genitals and the tail. The גמרא limits the pouch blemish to damage, not full removal, because a removed pouch can grow back. Finally it defines the 'fingerbreadth' as a quarter of a טפח. רבה says this measure was taught for ציצית, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע begins a different answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A blemish after slaughter but before collecting the blood disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier answer with רב's rule that cutting the bull's ear after שחיטה but before קבלה makes it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי זירא said in the name of רב: if someone slits the bull's ear and only afterward collects its blood, the offering is disqualified. The פסוק says 'from the blood of the bull,' meaning the bull as it already was, whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous answer. It shows that a defect appearing after שחיטה can still disqualify a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier approach assumed that a defect showing up after שחיטה does not matter. רב teaches that if a מום appears before the blood is collected, the קרבן is פסול. The פסוק calls it 'the bull,' meaning it must still be the same perfect bull it was before.

keyTerms.meaning: one who slits or nicks (here, the ear), creating a blemish
collecting the blood of the קרבן in a vessel
disqualified as a קרבן
the bull as it already was before

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabbi Zeira say that Rav says:
One who slits the ear of the bull
and afterward collected its blood —
it is disqualified, as it says: "And he shall take from the blood of the bull"
— the bull as it already was!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given at the end of the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier assumption that a defect after שחיטה does not disqualify.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that a מום made after שחיטה but before קבלה does disqualify, so the line cannot be drawn at שחיטה.

steps.title: The new line: before or after collecting the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a defect before קבלה disqualifies, but a defect after קבלה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, one source is talking about an animal that became lacking before the blood was collected. The other is talking about one that became lacking after the blood was collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. It moves the deciding moment from שחיטה to קבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer fits רב's rule, since his case is a defect before קבלה. A defect after קבלה is treated as not disqualifying. That way the two sources about the missing כוליא no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: rather — drops the old answer and gives a new one
here... there — splits the two sources into different cases
it became lacking (missing a part)

phrases.english: Rather: here, it is where it became lacking before the collection,
there, it is where it became lacking after the collection.
phrases.notes: In both sources being compared, the missing part is the כוליא (kidney).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the challenged answer with a new distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line was drawn at שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line is drawn at קבלה: before it, a defect disqualifies; after it, it does not.
steps.whatToRemember: The new answer: a defect before קבלה disqualifies, and a defect after קבלה does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the offering must stay perfect until the blood is sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer with a ברייתא saying the קרבן פסח must be תמים through קבלה, הולכה and זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a defect after collecting the blood but before throwing it really allowed? A ברייתא says: 'A perfect lamb, a male in its first year, it shall be for you' means perfect and in its first year at שחיטה. How do we know this also applies at collecting, carrying and sprinkling the blood? From the word 'shall be': all its stages must be perfect and in its first year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 2. It quotes a ברייתא showing the animal must stay perfect even after קבלה, all the way to זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said a defect after קבלה does not matter. This ברייתא learns from the word 'יהיה' that every stage of the עבודה, including זריקה, needs the animal תמים. If so, a defect between קבלה and זריקה should disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: throwing or sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
is it permitted? — here asked as a challenge
carrying the blood to the מזבח
all of its stages (from the word 'יהיה')

steps.confusionAlert: Although it starts like a question ('is it permitted?'), this is really an attack on step 2, backed by a ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר קַבָּלָה קוֹדֶם זְרִיקָה, מִי שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: And after collection but before sprinkling, is it permitted?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׂה תָּמִים זָכָר בֶּן שָׁנָה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם״,
phrases.english: "A perfect lamb, a male in its first year, it shall be for you,"

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא תָּמִים בֶּן שָׁנָה בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה.
phrases.english: meaning it must be perfect and in its first year at the time of slaughter.
And from where do we know this also applies at collection, carrying and sprinkling?
The verse says: "it shall be,"

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהוּ כׇּל הֲוָיוֹתָיו תָּם וּבֶן שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: so that at all its stages it is perfect and in its first year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַחַר קַבָּלָה קוֹדֶם זְרִיקָה, מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a defect after קבלה does not disqualify.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires the animal to be תמים even at הולכה and זריקה, which come after קבלה.

steps.title: Only the age requirement lasts until sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא's word 'יהיה' extends only the 'בן שנה' requirement to all the stages, not the 'תמים' requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain the ברייתא as referring to 'in its first year' only.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 3. It narrows what the ברייתא is saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's teaching that 'all its stages' count applies only to the age rule. The animal must still be in its first year at זריקה, but being תמים is required only until קבלה. So step 2's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: he explained it (read the source in a narrower way)
in its first year (the age requirement)

phrases.english: He explained it as referring to "in its first year" alone,
phrases.notes: Only the age rule lasts until the blood is sprinkled; being blemish-free is not part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requires both תמים and בן שנה through זריקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only בן שנה is required through זריקה; תמים is required only until קבלה.

steps.title: Support from רבי יהושע: blood is thrown if a כזית remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its reading with רבי יהושע's rule that the blood is thrown as long as a כזית of meat or fat remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהושע says: for every קרבן in the תורה, if a כזית of meat or a כזית of fat is left, the כהן throws the blood. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that the step 4 reading is correct. Losing parts of the animal after קבלה does not stop the זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע allows זריקה even when almost the whole animal is gone, as long as a כזית remains. If a huge loss after קבלה does not matter, a missing part like a כוליא certainly does not. That shows being תמים is not required at זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: so too it is logical — introduces support
an olive's volume, the minimum amount
learn from it — the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: Conclusion: a defect after קבלה does not disqualify the קרבן. Only the age requirement continues until זריקה, as רבי יהושע's כזית rule shows.
steps.whyThisMatters: It fixes קבלה as the moment after which damage to the animal no longer stops the blood from being thrown.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings in the Torah
from which there remains an olive's volume of meat
or an olive's volume of fat —
he throws the blood,
learn from this.
phrases.notes: Even if most of the animal is gone after the blood is collected, it is still not disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that being תמים is not required after קבלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהושע: the blood is thrown if a כזית of meat or fat remains.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A defect that appears after קבלה does not disqualify the קרבן.

steps.title: How can an animal pass its first year between slaughter and collecting the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the reading from step 4, that the age rule of בן שנה applies at קבלה and הולכה too. How could an animal be in its first year at שחיטה and already in its second year moments later?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there really such a case, where the animal is within its first year when it is slaughtered, and already in its second year when the blood is collected and carried?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own earlier reading. Why would the ברייתא need to say the animal must be בן שנה at קבלה and הולכה, when those happen only minutes after שחיטה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the גמרא said the word 'יהיה' stretches the בן שנה requirement to every stage of the עבודה. But the gap between שחיטה and קבלה is tiny. So the requirement seems pointless, unless an animal can 'age out' within those minutes.

keyTerms.meaning: Within its first year; the age requirement of the קרבן פסח
Slaughtering the animal
Collecting the blood in a vessel
Carrying the blood to the מזבח

phrases.english: But is there anything
where at the time of slaughter it is within its first year,
but at the time of collecting and carrying the blood
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 3, as the גמרא read it in step 4.

phrases.english: it is in its second year?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the reading of 'יהיה' from step 4 describes a case that can actually happen.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that בן שנה must hold at קבלה, הולכה and זריקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stages are only minutes apart, so the animal's age cannot realistically change between them.

steps.title: רבא: age for sacrifices is counted down to the hour
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the ברייתא that an animal's age for קדשים is counted to the exact hour. So an animal really can pass its first year between שחיטה and קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches us that hours disqualify in sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The ברייתא itself shows that age is measured to the exact hour, so the case can really happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the year ends at a precise hour, then the animal's first year can run out in the short time between שחיטה and קבלה. The ברייתא's ruling is therefore not pointless. It teaches that such an animal becomes פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is to say': a rule we learn from the source just quoted
Hours disqualify: age is counted to the exact hour
Sacrificial animals

steps.whatToRemember: For קרבנות, an animal's year is counted from the exact hour of its birth. Even a few hours can make it too old.

phrases.english: Rava said:
That is to say
hours disqualify in sacrifices.
phrases.notes: He means the year ends at the very hour the animal was born, not at the end of that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing that the case it doubted can really happen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning a new rule from the source itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Age changes only by whole days, so it could not change between שחיטה and קבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Age is counted by hours, so the animal can pass its first year in that short gap.

steps.title: Suggesting the internal-lack question is a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier question of whether an internal defect counts as a lack. It brings a ברייתא on ויקרא 22:24, where רבי יהודה says the four blemishes are all in the testicles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute of תנאים: 'And bruised, crushed, torn, and cut': all of them refer to the testicles. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It suggests that the earlier question was already argued by תנאים, and it starts quoting the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testicles are less exposed than the גיד. If damage there disqualifies the animal, that suggests a hidden or internal defect also counts. The full meaning of the ברייתא comes out over the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us say it is like the תנאים': a suggestion that an issue is already a dispute of תנאים
Bruised, crushed, torn, cut: the blemishes listed in ויקרא 22:24
Testicles

phrases.english: Let us say it is a dispute of Tannaim:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the earlier question of whether a lack inside the body counts as a lack.

phrases.english: 'And bruised, and crushed,'
'and torn, and cut'
— all of them are in the testicles,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about age and goes back to the main question of internal defects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the four blemishes of ויקרא 22:24 apply to the testicles.

steps.title: Only the testicles and not the גיד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה really means these blemishes count only in the testicles and not on the גיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the testicles and not on the גיד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי יהודה's statement. It is hard to believe he would leave out the גיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גיד is more exposed than the testicles. If damage to the testicles is a blemish, damage to the גיד should surely be one too. So 'all of them in the testicles' cannot mean 'only in the testicles'.

keyTerms.meaning: The male organ (penis)

phrases.english: In the testicles and not on the penis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי יהודה's statement quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'כולן בביצים' in רבי יהודה's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes no sense for blemishes to count in a hidden place but not in an exposed one.

steps.title: Correcting רבי יהודה's words to 'also in the testicles'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording so that רבי יהודה says the blemishes count also in the testicles, in addition to the גיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'Also in the testicles.' These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבי יהודה's wording to answer the question in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the correction, רבי יהודה agrees the גיד counts, and he adds the testicles as well. This is what makes him the opinion that is strict even about the less visible place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say': the גמרא changes the wording of a source
Also, even

phrases.english: Say: also in the testicles
phrases.notes: So the ברייתא now means: on the גיד, and also in the testicles.

phrases.english: — the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה counts the blemishes only in the testicles.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה counts them on the גיד and also in the testicles.

steps.title: The other opinions: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says all four blemishes count only on the גיד. רבי יוסי says bruised and crushed count in the testicles too, but torn and cut count only on the גיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: all of them are on the גיד. רבי יוסי says: bruised and crushed apply also to the testicles; torn and cut count on the גיד, yes, but in the testicles, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא, which gives two more opinions. This sets up the question in the next step about what they are arguing over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three opinions. רבי יהודה counts all four blemishes in the testicles too. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב counts none of them in the testicles. רבי יוסי counts two of them in the testicles and not the other two.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes / no

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
All of them are on the penis.
Rabbi Yosei says:
'Bruised and crushed' — also in the testicles,
'torn and cut' — on the penis, yes,
in the testicles, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן בַּגִּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that step 8 began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: only on the גיד. רבי יוסי: bruised and crushed also in the testicles; torn and cut only on the גיד.

steps.title: Is the dispute about whether an internal lack counts as a lack?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the תנאים argue over the earlier question. One holds that a lack inside the body is called a חסרון, and the other holds it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this: one master holds that a lack on the inside is called a lack, and the other master holds it is not called a lack?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now ties the ברייתא back to its main question. It suggests the תנאים are really arguing about whether an internal lack counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה, who counts blemishes in the testicles, would hold that a hidden lack counts as a חסרון. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who counts only the exposed גיד, would hold that it does not. If this is right, the earlier question is a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it not that...?': introduces a suggested explanation
They disagree
A lack on the inside of the body
One master holds

steps.whyThisMatters: If this suggestion is right, the earlier question about a lack inside the body was already argued by תנאים, and each possible answer has a תנא behind it.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, who counts blemishes in the testicles too.

phrases.english: a lack on the inside is called a lack,
and the other master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who counts only the גיד.

phrases.english: it is not called a lack?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the ברייתא in steps 8–11 has to do with the internal-lack question.
steps.raayaObject: That whether an internal lack counts as a חסרון is already a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי יוסי on ויקרא 22:24

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view does not fit the suggested argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the תנאים argue over whether an internal lack is called a חסרון, because רבי יוסי's split view fits neither side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really explain it that way? Then what does רבי יוסי hold? If he holds that a lack inside the body counts as a lack, then torn and cut should count too. And if he holds it does not count as a lack, then bruised and crushed should not count either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion from Step 12. It shows that רבי יוסי does not fit that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four blemishes are hidden inside the scrotum. So if the argument were only about internal lacks, רבי יוסי would have to treat all four the same way. He counts two and not the other two, so the argument must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really understand it that way? (an opening that pushes back on an idea)
A lack on the inside of the body, one that cannot be seen
He holds

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?
What does Rabbi Yosei hold?
If he holds that a lack on the inside
is called a lack
then even "torn and cut" should count too!
And if he holds it is not called a lack
then even "bruised and crushed" should not count either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation suggested in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the ברייתא's argument is about whether an internal lack counts as a חסרון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's split ruling cannot match either position, since all four blemishes are equally internal.

steps.title: New explanation: they argue about visible blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about which blemishes can be seen. רבי יהודה says all four show because the testicles shrink or hang. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says none clearly show, because healthy testicles also sometimes shrink or hang.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they argue about blemishes that can be seen. רבי יהודה holds that bruised and crushed is a blemish, because the testicles shrink. Torn and cut is a blemish, because they hang down. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that bruised and crushed is not a blemish, because even healthy testicles sometimes shrink. Torn and cut is not a blemish, because even healthy testicles sometimes hang.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to understand the argument. According to רש״י, everyone now agrees that a lack inside the body counts as a lack; they argue about whether these outward signs are a visible blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is now how the damage looks from the outside, not whether an internal lack counts. רבי יהודה treats shrinking and hanging as clear signs of damage. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says these signs prove nothing, because healthy animals show them too.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemishes that can be seen from the outside
They argue
They shrink or pull in
They hang down
From the start, before any damage

phrases.english: Rather, here
they argue about blemishes that can be seen
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
"bruised and crushed" is a blemish
because they shrink
"torn and cut" is a blemish
because they hang down
phrases.notes: Once torn loose inside, the testicles dangle lower than normal, and you can see that.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov holds:
"bruised and crushed" is not a blemish
because even beforehand, they sometimes shrink
"torn and cut" is not a blemish
because even beforehand, they sometimes hang down

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in Step 13 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the argument is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue over whether an internal lack is called a חסרון.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue over whether the outward signs (shrinking, hanging) clearly show a blemish.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 12. The internal-lack explanation has been dropped. The argument is now only about what can be seen.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's middle view explained
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי counts bruised and crushed because the testicles are truly gone. He does not count torn and cut because the testicles are still there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי holds that bruised and crushed is a blemish, because the testicles are no longer there. Torn and cut is not a blemish, because the testicles are still there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its new explanation by showing how רבי יוסי fits into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushed testicles are destroyed, so something is truly missing. Torn or cut testicles stay in the pouch even though they no longer work, so nothing is missing. This solves the problem from Step 13, where רבי יוסי's split view did not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not there
They are there

steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation is that the תנאים argue about visible blemishes. רבי יהודה counts all four. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב counts none. רבי יוסי counts only the ones where the testicles are truly gone.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
"bruised and crushed" is a blemish
because they are not there
phrases.notes: He means the testicles are smashed, so they no longer exist in their normal form.

phrases.english: "torn and cut" is not a blemish
because they are still there

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the new explanation from Step 14 by explaining רבי יוסי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי's split view fits once the argument is about visible blemishes. Missing testicles are a blemish, and testicles that are still present are not.

steps.title: New משנה: blemishes of the pouch, genitals, and tail
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more blemishes: damage to the pouch, to a female's genitals, to the tail at the bone (but not at a joint), a split tail tip, and flesh a fingerbreadth long between tail vertebrae.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the pouch was damaged, or the genitals of a female sacrificial animal; if the tail was damaged at the bone but not at the joint; or if the tip of the tail is split, meaning the skin and flesh peeled off and the bone remained; or if there is a full fingerbreadth of flesh from one vertebra to the next. All these are blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and continues the list of blemishes that allow a בכור to be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds blemishes in two areas: the private parts and the tail. For the tail, it is exact about where the damage is. Damage at the bone counts, but damage at a joint does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The pouch that holds the male's genitals
Genitals (here, of a female animal)
A joint between the bones of the tail
A vertebra, one bone section of the tail
A full fingerbreadth

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If the pouch was damaged
or the genitals of a female, among sacrificial animals
if the tail was damaged from the bone
but not from the joint
or the end of the tail is split
the skin and the flesh peeled off
and the bone remained
or there is flesh from one vertebra to the next
a full fingerbreadth

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the testicle discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damage to the pouch or a female's genitals, damage to the tail at the bone (not at a joint), a split tail tip with exposed bone, and a fingerbreadth of flesh between tail vertebrae are all blemishes.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the pouch blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the pouch blemish counts only when the pouch is damaged, not removed, and only the pouch, not the male organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבי אלעזר says: It was damaged, but not removed. The pouch, but not the male organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by having רבי אלעזר narrow the משנה's rule about a damaged pouch (כיס) on a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said a damaged pouch is a מום. רבי אלעזר adds two limits. First, it must be damaged, not fully removed. Second, the damage must be to the pouch, not to the male organ itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Was damaged or nicked
Was removed completely
The pouch or sheath around the male organ
The male organ itself

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that damage is a blemish but full removal is not. Step 19 explains why: a removed pouch can grow back.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar says:
It was damaged, but not removed.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the pouch from the משנה in step 16.

phrases.english: The pouch, but not the male organ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: נִפְגַּם וְלֹא נִיטַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the pouch blemish listed in the משנה in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pouch blemish applies only to damage, not full removal, and only to the pouch, not the male organ.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted with the exact same two limits as רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: It was damaged, but not removed. The pouch, but not the male organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי אלעזר by showing that a ברייתא teaches the very same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not add a new rule. It shows that רבי אלעזר's limits are not only his own idea, because an earlier teaching says the same words.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
It was damaged, but not removed.
The pouch, but not the male organ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's statement from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's two limits on the pouch blemish
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: A pouch torn off by a wolf grew back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן המשולם tells of an animal whose pouch a wolf tore off, and it grew back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן המשולם says: There was an incident with one animal in עינבל. A wolf removed its pouch, and it went back to full strength.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יוסי בן המשולם tells a real story that shows why a fully removed pouch is not a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מום has to be lasting. Since a removed pouch can grow back, as in this story, full removal is not a permanent blemish. That explains the 'not removed' limit from steps 17 and 18.

keyTerms.meaning: A real incident or story
Wolf
Went back to its full strength; here, it grew back

steps.whatToRemember: The pouch blemish counts only when the pouch is damaged, not removed, because a removed pouch can grow back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
There was an incident with one animal in Inbal,
phrases.notes: עינבל is the name of a place.

phrases.english: where a wolf removed it,
and it returned to its strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּעִינְבָּל אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case showing why full removal of the pouch is not a blemish.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a removed pouch is not a blemish
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident in עינבל, where a pouch grew back after a wolf tore it off

steps.title: How big is a fingerbreadth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the tail blemish, and a תנא defines the אצבע as one quarter of an average person's טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If the tail was damaged from the bone, and so on. A תנא taught: The fingerbreadth they spoke of is one of four in a handbreadth of an average person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, about the tail, and brings a teaching that defines the 'fingerbreadth' mentioned there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said flesh one אצבע long between tail vertebrae is a מום. Fingers differ in size, so the תנא gives a standard measure: one quarter of an average person's טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Tail
Fingerbreadth, a unit of measure
Handbreadth, equal to four fingerbreadths
A teacher from the time of the משנה taught

phrases.english: The tail was damaged from the bone, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 16; 'etc.' points to the fingerbreadth of flesh between the joints.

phrases.english: A תנא taught: The fingerbreadth that they spoke of
is one of four in a handbreadth
of any average person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the pouch to the tail blemish in the משנה and defines its measurement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אצבע is one quarter of an average person's טפח.

steps.title: Which law was this measure taught for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which הלכה this definition of the אצבע was taught for.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law was this taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next steps: which law was this definition of the אצבע taught for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא's wording, 'the fingerbreadth that they spoke of,' sounds like a general rule. So the גמרא wants to know which specific law it was first said about.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? Which הלכה is this about?

phrases.english: With regard to what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the definition from step 20 comes from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which הלכה the definition of the אצבע was taught for

steps.title: רבה: it was taught for the strings of ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the measure was taught for תכלת. He quotes a ברייתא where בית שמאי say four strings and בית הלל say three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: It is about תכלת. As it was taught: How many strings does one put on? בית שמאי say four, and בית הלל say three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the definition was taught about תכלת, and starts quoting the ברייתא that shows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first gives the argument about how many strings go on the garment. This sets up its next line, which talks about length in fingerbreadths.

keyTerms.meaning: The blue thread; here it means the ציצית strings
Strings or threads
The students of שמאי
The students of הלל

phrases.english: Rabba says: With regard to תכלת,
as it was taught: How many strings does one put on?
בית שמאי say: Four,
and בית הלל say: Three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אצבע measure was taught about תכלת (ציצית).

steps.title: The ציצית ברייתא uses the same measure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: the hanging part is four fingerbreadths according to בית שמאי and three according to בית הלל, and each fingerbreadth is one quarter of an average person's טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much should hang down? בית שמאי say four, and בית הלל say three. And the three that בית הלל say are each one of four in a handbreadth of an average person.
steps.whatsHappening: The rest of the ברייתא gives the exact wording that רבה pointed to, which proves his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last line uses the same words as the תנא in step 20: 'one of four in a handbreadth of an average person.' This shows the definition was first said for the length of the ציצית strings.

keyTerms.meaning: Hanging down; the free part of the strings past the knots
Here, the three fingerbreadths that בית הלל require

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, the definition 'one quarter of a טפח' comes from the ציצית ברייתא and is also used for the tail blemish.

phrases.english: And how much should be hanging down?
בית שמאי say: Four,
and בית הלל say: Three.
And the three that בית הלל say
are each one of four in a handbreadth
of any average person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא רבה quoted and shows the matching wording.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that the אצבע definition was taught about תכלת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ציצית ברייתא, which uses the same words as the תנא

steps.title: A second answer: the two measuring cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a different answer: the definition was taught about the two measuring cubits, and he begins quoting a משנה about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, says: It is about the two cubits, as we learned: There were two cubits...
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another answer to the question in step 21 and starts quoting his source, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagrees with רבה about where the definition comes from. He links it to the two measuring rods of an אמה described in a משנה, not to ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: Cubit, a unit of length

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, says:
It is about the two cubits,
as we learned: There were two cubits
phrases.notes: These are two measuring rods. The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: לִשְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 21's question than רבה gave in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אצבע definition was taught about the two measuring cubits.
